sites.name: Abu Galawa Kebir

s1.quote: The Chinese barge named Tien Hsing sank in 1943 and lays between 5 m and 18 m depth directly at the reef

s2.quote: Type of vessel: Tug boat … Maximum depth: Wreck: 0 to 17 meters, reef: 35 meters

summary.text: Small Chinese vessel sunk in 1943 on the Abu Galawa Kebir reef in the Fury Shoals. It lies shallow, roughly 5 to 18 m, and has long since grown into the reef, with the reef itself falling to about 35 m.

sites.depthNote: Wreck 5-18 m; surrounding reef to about 35 m

s1.quote: Lying on its side in just 14m of water, Hamada is a fairly easy, extremely picturesque dive site. Depth: 6m to 14m. Rating: novice.

s2.quote: the Hamada, is at 14 meters of water at Abo Ghosum reef … Abu Ghosum is a site that suits divers of all levels of experience … so parts of the wreck are so shallow that you can even snorkel them … the propeller who is still intact

highlights.text: Parts shallow enough to snorkel
Intact propeller

summary.text: A roughly 65 m cargo ship lying on its side on an inshore reef at Abu Ghosum south of Marsa Alam, in only about 14 m of water. Easy and photogenic, suitable for all experience levels.

s1.quote: is a tourist town in south-eastern Egypt, located on the western shore of the Red Sea

s1.quote: are two small Red Sea islands in the Red Sea Governorate of Egypt

notDiveSite.reason: Two Red Sea islands (the Brothers) containing many separate dive sites

s1.quote: off Port Said , the German submarine U-372 fired two torpedoes that sank Medway

notDiveSite.reason: HMS Medway sank in the Mediterranean off Port Said (about 32.05N 30.92E); this pin is inland in the Nile Delta, and Egypt-labelled Red Sea/fresh water does not apply

s1.quote: She rests on her starboard side on a flat sand bottom at 27m of depth, with the shallowest section at just 7m … Reef Summary Depth 12 - 27m Visibility 15 - 30m Currents Can be strong … Experience level Intermediate - advanced … Lying on the sea floor are everyday personal items such as a handbag

s2.quote: The wreck rests on her starboard side in 30 meters of Red Sea water. It is a spooky and controversial dive at a maritime grave. Many dive guides refuse to dive the Salem Express. Penetration is not considered a no-go zone but frowned upon

s3.quote: lying on its port side in 30 meters/100 ft of seawater … we first saw the two giant propellers and the rudder

penetration.value: Penetration frowned upon; many guides refuse as it is a maritime grave

highlights.text: Two giant propellers and rudder
Personal items still lie on the seabed

hazards.text: Memorial wreck; many guides will not dive it

summary.text: A ferry lost in 1991 near Safaga, now on her side on sand with her highest point near 7 m and her deepest about 27 to 30 m. A sombre, advanced boat dive on a grave site, where penetration is discouraged.

s1.quote: wrecks sit at various depths within recreational limits (roughly 5 to 32 meters) … The current can be strong and usually runs from north to south … Generally excellent, often exceeding 20–30 meters … accessible for both day boats and liveaboards … The stern section lies at a 45-degree angle, resting on its port side at about 24 meters deep

s2.quote: rising to 12m at the bow … slid off the reef into 30-32m of water … which gives the wreck its nickname Tile Wreck … Coral growth is profuse because the wreck has been down almost 150 years

s3.quote: At least four complete wrecks lie here … Abu Nuhas is exposed to current and wind

highlights.text: Giannis D stern tilted at 45 degrees
Chrisoula K tile cargo in the holds
Carnatic wreck heavily coral-encrusted

hazards.text: Exposed reef; wind and swell make mooring hard

summary.text: A reef at the mouth of the Gulf of Suez that has claimed at least four large ships, among them the Carnatic, Giannis D, Chrisoula K and Kimon M, lying within a few hundred metres at roughly 5 to 32 m. Exposed to wind and current.

s1.quote: Depth: 29 M Difficulty: Intermediate Type: Drift dive, Wreck … now lies with the top of bow at 15 metres and the stern on the sea bed at 29 metres

s2.quote: rests at a depth of 30 meters adjacent to the reef wall. The wreck is entirely inverted and split into two sections. The stern section of the Dunraven is around 29 meters deep … The exit area is filled with thousands of glass fish

s3.quote: She now lies at a depth of between 15 and 30 metres

highlights.text: Inverted hull with swim-through by the boiler
Thousands of glassfish at the exit

summary.text: The Dunraven sank in 1876 on the Beacon Rock reef at the northwest edge of Ras Mohammed and now lies upside down in two sections, from about 15 m at the bow to 29-30 m at the stern, heavily encrusted with coral and glassfish.

s1.quote: sits upright on the seabed at 33m … Reef Summary Depth 16 - 33m Visibility 15 - 25m Currents Can be strong … Experience level Intermediate - advanced … it is possible to swim through the wreck from Hold 1 to 3, using the internal interconnecting doorways at a maximum depth of 25m … BSA motorbikes, Morris automobiles, Bedford trucks

s2.quote: The depth of around 30 m (100 feet) at its deepest is ideal for diving

penetration.value: Holds 1 to 3 can be swum through at up to 25 m

highlights.text: BSA motorbikes, trucks and cars in the holds
Ship largely intact, upright on sand

summary.text: A British freighter bombed in 1941 and now sitting upright on sand at about 30 m in the Gulf of Suez, with her wartime cargo of vehicles and motorbikes still stowed in the holds. A deep, advanced boat dive.

s1.quote: Depth: 0-30 M Difficulty: Intermediate … plateau at 25 metres with a row of huge fan corals … currents can be strong at the most northerly tip of the reef

s2.quote: The reef reaches from 0.5 to 28m where it forms a plateau

s3.quote: large plateaus at around 82 feet, (25 m) on the southeastern side, can feature sleeping sharks in the sandy areas … there are usually strong currents on the southern and northern ends of the reef

s4.quote: The lack of mooring points makes drift diving necessary here … you descend down a wall splendidly covered in gorgonians, whip corals and black corals, and arrive at a large ledge at 25m depth, where you can often find resting whitetip reef sharks and leopard sharks

highlights.text: Plateau with a row of large gorgonian fans
Whitetip and leopard sharks on the ledge

hazards.text: Strong currents at the north and south ends
Thomas Canyon runs to 90 m; technical divers only

summary.text: The smallest and most colourful of the four Tiran reefs, dived as a drift along a wall of gorgonians to a plateau near 25 m, with sharks resting on the ledge. Currents can be strong at either end.

s1.quote: Depth: 0-30 M Difficulty: Intermediate … The longest and narrowest of the four reefs in Tiran stretching approx. 1 kilometre in length

s2.quote: Starting in the south there is a wall to about 98 feet (30 m) with coral growth all the way down from the surface … a canyon at the halfway point, 82 feet (25 m), where you will start to notice the current strengthen … Washing Machine — so called due to the very strong currents in all directions

s3.quote: a wall that starts from the surface, reaching about 45m

s4.quote: no shelter or fixed moorings for dive boats, and diving here is a drift from south to north

mooring.value: No fixed moorings; drift south to north

highlights.text: Wall running from the surface down
Giant morays, groupers, barracuda and jacks

hazards.text: "Washing Machine" currents between Woodhouse and Jackson

summary.text: The longest reef in the Straits of Tiran, a wall dropping from the surface to about 30 m or more, dived as a south-to-north drift with a canyon midway. Currents build toward the north end where it meets Jackson Reef.

s1.quote: a shallow hard coral lagoon (10-12m), known as Laguna Reef … susceptible to strong tidal flows which dictate dive plans

s2.quote: A drift dive around the outer wall of the South Laguna of Tiran island … This is a dive for all levels

hazards.text: Strong tidal flows dictate the dive plan

summary.text: A shallow hard-coral lagoon on the west of Tiran island, split in two by a coral wall into North and South Laguna, with a drift along the outer wall suited to all levels. Tidal flow controls when and how it is dived.

s1.quote: the Canyon is a long, narrow trench that runs perpendicular to the reef shelf … Depth: 5m to 33m. Rating: intermediate. Access: shore.

s2.quote: Depth: 0-30 M Difficulty: Intermediate … the penetration point, which is at around 15 metres … The canyon itself is a cave with an open ceiling … We slowly descend into the canyon from 18 to 30 metres

s3.quote: A great site for octopus, stonefish and devil scorpion fish … deep fissure in the reef … filled with light shafts and over hangs where glassfish and cave sweepers reside

highlights.text: Open-topped canyon with glassfish and light shafts
Octopus, stonefish and scorpionfish

summary.text: A shore dive north of Dahab that crosses a shallow lagoon and coral garden to a deep open-topped fissure in the reef, filled with glassfish and lit by shafts of light. Intermediate level, roughly 5 to 30 m.

sites.name: Blue Hole

s1.quote: Depth range 6 to 100 m … maximum depth within the hole of just over 100 m … Entry type Shore … there is frequently a current flowing inward through the arch into the Blue Hole … Local dive centres take appropriately qualified divers to 30 m

s2.quote: the famous Blue hole dive site is a large submarine sinkhole, 150m across and 110m deep

highlights.text: Saddle opening to the sea at about 6 m
Popular freediving venue

hazards.text: The Arch (ceiling 55 m) has killed many divers

summary.text: A circular sinkhole on the Gulf of Aqaba shore north of Dahab, just over 100 m deep, reached by walking in. Recreational divers keep to about 30 m on the Bells route; the Arch at 55 m is a notorious technical hazard.

sites.depthNote: Hole just over 100 m; Arch ceiling at 55 m

s1.quote: Depth: 0-30 M Difficulty: Intermediate … The chimney closes at around 23 metres but divers can continue down to the next opening at 26-28 metres … at about 18 metres there is a cleaner fish family

s2.quote: The Bells entry is from the shore … Local dive centres take appropriately qualified divers to 30 m … At 26 m at the bottom of the Bells is a mini arch that should not be confused with the arch in the Blue Hole

highlights.text: Chimney descent lit by sun rays
Cleaner fish station at about 18 m

hazards.text: Narrow chimney entry; mini arch at 26 m is not the Arch

summary.text: A shore entry through a narrow reef chimney that exits onto a wall at about 26-28 m, then follows the wall to the saddle into the Blue Hole. Guided centres take qualified divers to 30 m.
